title: Reading what a level will hold
target: What decides how much loot and how many monsters a level in R.E.P.O. sends, so a run can be planned around the level rather than discovered halfway through it.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Some idea of the level's theme
A crew that can split up

steps.do: Expect the loot to be decided by the level, not by luck alone.
steps.because: a director decides the valuables in a level, with an amount curve for each size (ValuableDirector, tinyMaxAmountCurve1, smallMaxAmountCurve1, mediumMaxAmountCurve1, bigMaxAmountCurve1, wideMaxAmountCurve1, tallMaxAmountCurve1, veryTallMaxAmountCurve1)

steps.do: Treat each size of valuable as having its own chance as well as its own amount.
steps.because: each size has a chance of its own beside its amount (tinyChance, smallChance, mediumChance, bigChance, wideChance, tallChance, veryTallChance)

steps.do: Plan around a changing level rather than a fixed one.
steps.because: each size has a second amount curve and the total value of a level has two curves of its own (tinyMaxAmountCurve2, veryTallMaxAmountCurve2, totalMaxValueCurve1, totalMaxValueCurve2)

steps.do: Pick the difficulty with the monster count in mind.
steps.because: the level has an enemy director with three difficulty settings of its own (EnemyDirector, enemiesDifficulty1, enemiesDifficulty2, enemiesDifficulty3)

steps.do: Expect pressure to come in waves rather than steadily.
steps.because: each difficulty has its amount curves in pairs, with a curve for the pause between spawns (amountCurve1_1, amountCurve1_2, spawnIdlePauseCurve)

steps.do: Know that a monster is only allowed to stay for a while.
steps.because: there are two curves for how long it may stay before it despawns, and despawns decrease with time given in minutes and as a percentage (despawnTimeCurve_1, despawnTimeCurve_2, despawnedDecreaseMinutes, despawnedDecreasePercent)

steps.do: Remember that which monsters appear is set up separately from how many.
steps.because: an enemy set-up holds a list of things to spawn (EnemySetup, spawnObjects)

steps.do: Expect some monsters to be unlocked by progress rather than to be present from the first run.
steps.because: a set-up can be gated by levels completed with a lowest and a highest value, and it counts runs played (levelsCompletedCondition, levelsCompletedMin, levelsCompletedMax, runsPlayed)

commonMistakes: Assuming a quiet start means a quiet level.
Planning a full sweep when the level's monsters are gated by how far the crew has got.
Treating every size of valuable as equally likely.
Leaving the level early because a spawn wave ended, when the loot director is separate.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
